absent: Numeric values and widths of processor identity markers and scheduling flags and placement hints are not shown in these fragments.
Configuration conditions selecting among alternate no operation and boosted and iterator and warning variants are not shown.
Internals of unrouted switch stages and table handling and lazy reference handling and timer arming and virtual time calculation and signal handling are not shown.
Complete layouts of task and runqueue and fair and deadline and memory and statistics records beyond observed fields are not shown.

findings.text: schedule_tail provides first return for a freshly created task and finalizes the pending switch while holding then releasing the local runqueue lock, records scheduler exit tracing, reenables preemption, optionally publishes the thread identifier to user space, and recomputes pending signal state.

context_switch moves execution from a previous task to a next task on the same runqueue, prepares the switch, selects address space handling according to whether each side has user memory, propagates concurrency control state and processor local identity state, notifies restartable sequence tracking, performs the register and stack exchange with ordering enforcement, and then finalizes the previous task. The runqueue lock is held on entry and released through finalization.

Address space handling distinguishes four combinations. Transitions toward kernel execution use lazy table entry and retain the previous active space, acquiring an extra lazy reference when arriving from user execution and clearing the previous pointer otherwise. Transitions toward user execution propagate barrier state, switch tables with ordering guarantees, mark the new space as used, and when departing from kernel execution stash the borrowed active space in the runqueue for deferred release while clearing the previous pointer.

Barrier state propagation is skipped when previous and next memory descriptors are identical or when the runqueue already matches the next descriptor state. Otherwise the runqueue adopts the next descriptor state with single copy atomic accesses. An alternate build configuration provides an unconditional no operation.

Processor identity assignment on schedule in is skipped for inactive tasks. Active tasks read the current processor value and the configured mode, then follow a task owned path when the mode indicates task ownership or a processor owned path otherwise. Both paths prefer preserving an existing identifier when inside the configured maximum, otherwise attempt convergence into the optimal range, hand over or drop owned values, allocate a fresh value when empty, and propagate a transition marker when required. Task record updates notify restartable sequence tracking only when the value changes, while processor record updates are direct.

Identity handling on schedule out acts only when the outgoing task value carries a transition marker. If global transition has finished and the stripped value lies within the configured maximum, ownership is transferred and both task and processor records are aligned to enable a fast path on next entry. Otherwise the stripped value is released and the task value is marked unset. The combined switch helper invokes outgoing handling followed by incoming handling, with an alternate build providing an unconditional no operation.

Extensible scheduler exit first acquires a global task list lock with interrupt state preservation to detach list membership and optionally remove a hash entry, then separately acquires the task runqueue lock to adjust scheduler state. The two critical sections do not nest and the global lock is released before the runqueue lock is taken.

sched_ext_dead distinguishes three exit cases. Tasks with no scheduler association require no further action. Tasks observed starting initialization skip scheduler callbacks and move directly to dead so that a later recheck can cancel initialization. All other associated tasks invoke scheduler disable and exit callbacks under the runqueue lock before being marked dead, ensuring ordering against concurrent enable transitions and cgroup iteration.

System wide observability helpers aggregate per processor counters. Runnable total sums runnable counts across online processors. Local single task check tests whether the current processor runnable count equals one. Switch totals and input wait totals sum respective per processor counters across possible processors, with per processor accessors for individual values.

sched_exec queries the task scheduler class for a destination processor while holding the task priority protection lock. The request is abandoned when the destination equals the current processor or is not active. Otherwise execution is synchronously migrated by running a stop function on the source processor with task and destination as arguments.

Per processor accounting storage provides one kernel statistics record and one extended processor statistics record per processor, with idle sleep sequence initialization under a no tick configuration.

task_sched_runtime returns the stored execution total directly on wide word builds when the task is not on a processor or not in queued state. Otherwise the task runqueue is locked, and only when the task is both the donor current and queued are the runqueue clock refreshed and the current entity updated before sampling the total. A prefetch hint touches the fair current entity and its start stamp before the update.

Fair progress accounting ignores missing current entities and non positive deltas, accounts positive deltas to local runtime and to the fair service entity, advances virtual time and deadline for task entities, and always updates the fair server accounting. Queues with a single entity stop after accounting. Larger queues request lazy rescheduling and clear peer hints when the deadline indicates expiry or when the remaining slice is not protected.

Deadline service gating requires active state with non zero runtime, with early return for non positive deltas absent yield, for throttled deferrable servers without deferral, and for specially marked entities. Accounted execution reduces remaining runtime in scaled form for ordinary entities and unscaled form for servers, with defer idle markers cleared whenever not idle. Exhaustion while throttled and deferrable starts a new period with timer cancellation and restart and adjusted idle deferral, including a zero runtime park when waiting idle at zero laxity.

Exhaustion or yield moves the entity to throttled state with optional overrun recording when notification was requested, removal from deadline ordering and for ordinary tasks also from pushable tracking with statistics updates. Boosted entities or timer arming failures cause immediate replenishment or requeue, otherwise the entity awaits timer replenishment. Rescheduling is requested unless the entity remains earliest. Non service execution also contributes to shared real time bandwidth accounting under its lock when enabled.

Boost detection compares the priority inherited entity against the entity itself in one build and reports never boosted in an alternate build. Entity kind distinguishes ordinary tasks from fair service and extensible service when that class is configured and other service uses. Earliest determination tests whether the entity node is the first cached node in the deadline ordered tree.

Pushable deadline tracking maintains a per runqueue ordered tree with a cached earliest deadline. Removal is a no operation for nodes already detached, otherwise erases the node, refreshes the cached earliest value from the new leftmost when present, clears the node state, and when the tree becomes empty while marked overloaded clears the overload indication with shared count and mask updates provided the runqueue is online.

New period replenishment sets deadline to runqueue time plus the priority entity period and restores runtime from the priority entity budget, which equals the entity itself for non boosted tasks. Deferrable servers not already handling starvation enter throttled and armed states. A replenishment trace is recorded with entity kind and processor identity.

Switch ordering requires barrier state propagation before table switching when moving toward user execution, with a full ordering guarantee before returning to user space provided either by the table switch itself or by the final release path when address spaces match. Lazy reference acquisition and deferred release must pair across the switch and finalization to avoid leaking or prematurely dropping the borrowed space.

Sampling the on processor flag without locking is intentionally racy but safe because races with departure still take the lock while races with arrival correspond to earlier sampling with zero unaccounted time. Projecting execution for dequeued tasks would attribute cycles that may never be accounted and would break time queries, so both donor current status and queued status are required before refreshing the clock.

Execution time sampling serializes against enqueue and switch activity by locking the task runqueue, while placement selection serializes against priority changes by holding the task priority protection lock only during destination query and releasing it before synchronous migration.

Processor identity encoding uses distinct markers for processor ownership and transition mode and unset state to distinguish task owned values from processor owned values and transitional values during mode changes.

Observed runqueue state includes runnable counts, switch counts, wait counts, barrier state, stashed previous memory, fair and deadline subqueues with service entities, online status, identifier and domain membership, while observed task state includes user and active memory pointers, processor identity activity and value, extensible scheduler membership and hash linkage, deadline linkage and pushable node, scheduling class and placement lock, execution accumulators, and queue and processor presence flags.
